channel.title: Durga.design blog
channel.description: Battle-tested UX design insights, onboarding teardowns, and psychological frameworks for SaaS founders and engineers. Written by Senior Product Designer Durga Prasad.

item.title: I Built My First Framer Template. Here's Everything Nobody Tells You
item.description: Building a Framer template is closer to shipping a product than designing a website. What Callback taught me: build editable sections as components with props, test at in-between screen widths, make everything that looks clickable work, ask someone else to click through before you submit, and plan v1.1 before you ship v1.

item.title: Why Users Sign Up for Your SaaS and Never Come Back: How to Fix Onboarding Drop-Off in the First 5 Minutes
item.description: SaaS users drop off during onboarding when the product asks for effort before it gives any value: long signup forms, team invites and setup screens before they've seen the core feature. Cut signup to email and password, show sample data instead of an empty dashboard, and clearly confirm the first completed action.

item.title: The Pretty Design Trap: Why Minimalist B2B SaaS Dashboards Hurt Retention, and How to Design Dense Dashboards People Can Scan
item.description: Minimalist, whitespace-heavy dashboards hurt B2B SaaS retention because business users work under time pressure. Low-contrast grey text, actions hidden in unlabeled menus and only a few rows per screen slow every task down. Dense but well-organized tables, strong contrast and clear status labels make the product faster to use.

item.title: Pricing Page Psychology: Why Visitors Leave Your SaaS Pricing Page Without Buying, and How to Reduce Pricing Page Abandonment
item.description: Visitors leave SaaS pricing pages mostly because of unanswered anxiety, not price. They can't tell which plan fits them, they fear being trapped by auto-renewal, and they worry about looking foolish if it fails. Highlight one recommended plan, add honest reassurance under every button, and describe features as problems solved.

item.title: Fintech UX Design: How to Build Trust When People Hand You Their Money, with Clear Payment States, Upfront Fees and Honest Error Recovery
item.description: Fintech UX builds trust through clarity. Every payment state is explained in plain words, every fee is shown before the final tap, and every failed transaction says what happened, where the money is and what to do next. Predictable screens and honest numbers matter more than visual polish.

item.title: Cognitive Overload in B2B SaaS: How to Use Progressive Disclosure and Hick's Law to Simplify Complex Software Without Losing Power
item.description: Cognitive overload in B2B SaaS happens when a screen shows too many filters, buttons and fields at once. Hick's Law says decision time grows with the number of choices. Progressive disclosure fixes it: show the main workflow first, keep advanced controls one click away, use smart defaults and split long forms into steps.

item.title: The Anatomy of a High-Converting SaaS Landing Page: Clear Hero Headlines, Real Product Screenshots and Social Proof That Actually Works
item.description: A high-converting SaaS landing page tells visitors within about five seconds what the product is, who it's for and what changes for them. It shows the real product instead of abstract art, has one clear main call to action and backs its claims with specific social proof from real customers.

item.title: What a SaaS UX Audit Actually Uncovers: The Curse of Knowledge, the 4 Heuristic Lenses and How Findings Become a Prioritized Dev Roadmap
item.description: A SaaS UX audit reviews a product through usability heuristics such as information architecture, interaction cost, feedback and error prevention. It finds the friction founders and teams stop noticing because they know the product too well, and turns each finding into a list of fixes ranked by business impact and engineering effort.

item.title: Mobile UX for B2B SaaS: Why Enterprise Buyers Judge Your Product on Their Phone First, and the Mobile Experience You Actually Need
item.description: Mobile UX matters for B2B SaaS because decision-makers often discover and judge products on their phones, through LinkedIn, email or a colleague's link. A broken mobile page makes the product look careless. You don't need the full app on mobile, but you need a fast landing page, a way to continue on desktop and simple views for quick checks.

item.title: SaaS Microcopy That Increases Conversions: Button Text, Password Hints and Error Messages That Remove User Hesitation
item.description: Microcopy is the small text in an interface: button labels, hints under fields and error messages. Good SaaS microcopy tells people what happens when they click, shows the rules before they make a mistake and explains errors in plain words with a next step. These small changes reduce hesitation and help more people finish forms.

item.title: Consumer-Grade Enterprise Software: How to Design B2B Tools People Actually Enjoy Using, with Speed, Flexible Tables and Real Workflows
item.description: Consumer-grade enterprise software combines the reliability business-critical tools need with the speed and ease of good consumer apps. In practice, that means instant-feeling interactions, keyboard shortcuts, flexible data tables and navigation built around how people actually work. Tools people enjoy get adopted from the bottom up and defended at renewal.
